perspective:
I, Sara Manuelito, know or experienced:

- Shirley Whiteplume is my long-time colleague and close friend from our work together at a community health center.
- At a mutual patient’s funeral, I saw Shirley looking somber. I suspected she was deeply affected by the loss.
- I told Shirley I knew this must be hard and that I saw how much she cared for him. Shirley said it had been tough and she kept thinking if there was something more we could have done.
- I told her we did everything we could and should remember the good care and moments of joy we brought him. Shirley said I was right, but it was hard to let go.
- During a coffee break at work, I brought up the patient’s treatment and said I sensed Shirley might feel burdened by the outcome.
- Shirley told me she did feel responsible and wondered if pushing for a different approach might have given him a better chance.
- I told her we made the best decisions with the information we had, and that it was too heavy a burden to carry alone. Shirley said she appreciated it, but acceptance was hard.
- I noticed Shirley continued to be reserved and minimally expressive. In a quiet moment in our office, I confronted her, saying she had been holding back her feelings and it was okay to be open.
- Shirley told me she wasn’t sure she could and didn’t want to seem unprofessional or weak.
- I told her showing emotions doesn’t make her weak and is healthy, especially among friends. Shirley said maybe I was right and she would try to be more open.
- I later felt my previous confrontation might have been too harsh, so I apologized to Shirley if I came on too strong.
- Shirley told me it was a bit much but she knew I meant well and appreciated my apology.
- I told her I was there for her in whatever way she needed. Shirley thanked me and said we should keep talking because it helps.
- After some time, I noticed Shirley seemed to be doing a bit better. I asked how she was feeling.
- Shirley told me she was feeling better thanks to our talks and my support.
- I suggested spending more time together outside of work. Shirley said she would like that and suggested we plan something for the weekend.
